::JUDGMENT:

: 
This petition is filed by the Petitioner against Respondent No.1 & 2 under Sec.166 of M.V.Act 1989 for the relief of compensation.
SCCH-5 2

. The brief facts of the case is as under; That on 18.08.2022 at about 2.45 p.m. petitioner had been riding his Passion motor cycle bearing Reg.No.AP-39-AQ-6828 near Sudhakar Reddy fields on the way to Dodla Dairy, Palamaner Mandal, Chittoor, at that time, a Eicher bearing Reg.No.KA-37-7129 driven by its driver at high speed in rash and negligent manner and dashed against his motor cycle,
due to the impact, he fell down and sustained grievous injuries and his motor cycle was also badly damaged.

Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Government Hospital, Palamaner, after firstaid, he was shifted to Venkateshwara Institute of Medical Sciences, Tirupathi, wherein he took treatment as inpatient from 19.08.2022 to 26.08.2022, for which he has spent for Rs.2,50,000/-
towards hospitalization expenses.

entities.text: Venkateshwara Institute of Medical Sciences, Tirupathi
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: SCCH-5 3.
At the time of the accident he was aged about 31 years, hale and healthy, he was doing agricultural work and doing milk bending business, thereby earning Rs.30,000/- p.m.,
due to this accident he is not able to do his work till today and in future also.
Out of this accident crime No.245/2022 is registered against the driver of the Eicher vehicle before the Palamaner Urban Police for the offences punishable under Sec.337 of IPC.
Respondent No.1 is the R.C.Owner and R2 is the insurer of the said Eicher vehicle, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.

Hence, prays to allow the petition and grant compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 12% p.a.
4.
On service of notice, respondent No.1/owner has appeared and filed written statement.
Respondent No.1 submitted that, petitioner has fabricated the SCCH-5 documents and filed a false case against him.

Further submitted that, he is R.C.Owner and driver of the vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-37-7129 and in this regard RTO, Kolar has issued fitness certificate and the said vehicle is insured with respondent No.2 which is valid from 12.01.2022 to 11.01.2023.

Accordingly prays to Balakrishna Reddy.G vs G. Rakesh on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69941428/
2 dismiss the petition.

5. Respondent No.2/insurer has appeared and filed written statement and admitted issuance of policy bearing No.2317 2044 6558 3000 001 in respect of Eicher vehicle bearing Reg.No.
KA-37-7129 valid from 12.01.2022 to 11.01.2022 and liability if any, is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
Further submitted that, petition is filed through brother of the petitioner, in this regard, petitioner has not produced any expert opinion not obtained permission from this court.
Further SCCH-5 submitted that, petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary and proper party and he is entitled to take shelter under Sec.170 of M.V.Act.
There is no compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of M.V.Act claim made by the petitioner is higher, hence his petition is not maintainable.

Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.
6.

On going through the rival pleadings of the parties, my learned predecessor has framed the following:
::ISSUES::
1.

Whether Petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the motor vehicle accident that occurred on 18.08.2022 at about 2.45 p.m. when petitioner was riding his Passion Bike bearing Reg.No.AP-39-AQ-6828, near Sudhakar Reddy fields on the way of Dodla Dairy, Palamaner Mandal, Chitoor at that time, Eicher bearing Reg.No.KA-37-7129 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner dashed to the petitioner's motor cycle and caused accident, as mentioned in claim petition?
SCCH-5 2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so how much and from whom?
3. What order or award?

7. In order to prove his case, Petitioner brother as well as next friend has deposed his evidence as PW-1, examined Dr.Shailesh A.V. Rao as PW-2 and marked 15 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.15 and closed his evidence.
On the other hand, Legal Manager of respondent No.2 is examined as RW-1 and closed his evidence.

8. Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record, then my findings on the above issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final order for the  following:
 SCCH-5 Balakrishna Reddy.G vs G. Rakesh on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69941428/
3  ::REASONS::
9. Issue No.1:-
In order to prove his case, petitioner guardian as well as next friend has deposed his evidence as PW-1, in his chief-examination petitioner has reiterated the facts narrated in his petition.
Hence in order to avoid repetition of facts averments made in the evidence affidavit are not reiterated here.
In this regard copy of FIR is marked as Ex.P.1, copy of complaint is marked as Ex.P.2.

copy of sketch is marked as Ex.P.3, copy of list of charge sheet witnesses is marked as Ex.P.4,
copy of application filed for seeking permission to prosecute the case is marked as Ex.P.6, copy of charge sheet is marked as Ex.P.7.
10.
Further to substantiate the petitioner case, he examined one Doctor as PW-2.

On perusal of evidence of PW-1 and PW-2 and records those have marked i.e., as SCCH-5 FIR, complaint, sketch,
wound certificate, list of charge sheet witnesses, application for seeking permission to prosecute the case and charge sheet corroborates the case of the petitioner about causing of the accident dated 18.08.2022 as alleged in the petition and in the evidence of PW-1.
11.
On the other hand, Legal Manager of respondent No.2 is examined as RW-1.
Further except oral evidence, respondent No.2 has not taken any endeavors to disprove the petitioner's case about non- causing of the accident as alleged in the petition and evidence of PW-1.

Since in the absence of iota of evidence, I have no hesitation to believe the case of the petitioner about causing of the injuries to the petitioner out of the accident held on 18.08.2022 at about 2.45 p.m. while he was riding his Passionmc bearing SCCH-5 Reg.No.AP-39-AQ-6828 near Sudhakar Reddy fields on the way of Dodla Dairy, palamaner Mandal, Chittoor.
In the absence of iota of evidence, the arguments advanced by the petitioner's counsel are helpful to the case of the petitioner.
12. On the other hand, the police papers speaks that, very accident is occurred due to negligency of the car driver.

Under such circumstances, considering the said evidence and believing the evidence of the petitioner, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, petitioner has proved the above issue No.1 in his favour.
Accordingly I have answered above Issue No.1 in the affirmative.

13. Issue No.2:- As per the evidence of the petitioner, he had sustained left temporo parietal EDH +
left temporo parietal bone depressed fracture, CT Brain plain shows left temporo parietal EDH + left temporo SCCH-5 bone depressed fracture.

In this regard he has furnished copy of wound certificate marked as Ex.P. discharge summary marked as Ex.P.10 issued by Sri Venkateswara Institute of Medical Sciences, wherein he took treatment as indoor patient since 19.08.2022 to 26.08.2022.

14. Dr.Shailesh A.V.Rao, Consultant Neurosurgeon at Padmashree Diagnostic, Bengaluru is examined as PW-2 and he has exhibited OPD card marked as Ex.P.12, neuro physiologial assessment report marked as Ex.P.13, X-ray report along with mini mental state examination report marked as Ex.P.14 and disability certificate is marked as Ex.P.15 and he has assessed disability U/S E(11.1) amounts to a mRS score of 3, this amounts to a total disability around 60% and this disability is pertaining to whole body and is likely to be permanent.

In cross-examination he has categorically SCCH-5 admitted that, he has not treated the petitioner, GCS record will be entered in Balakrishna Reddy.G vs G. Rakesh on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69941428/

sentences.text: 4 followup records and recent GCS is 15 and it is normal.
Further deposed that, at the time of admission motor power is normal and at the time of discharge, there is improvement and there are no fresh trip sheets.

PW-2 deposed that, petitioner is quite well behaved man, he has answered to all the questions, his IQ value is not mentioned in discharge summary and as per the guidelines, if IQ is 58%, it is a mild disability and if IQ is above 69, there will be no cognitive disability.
Further deposed that, as per the discharge summary, petitioner was under the influence of alcohol and now the fractures are united.

Under such circumstances, considering the nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and also by relying on citation reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343 between Rajkumar V/s. Ajay Kumar, SCCH-5 the functional disability of the petitioner is considered at the rate of 20%,
for the purpose of calculation of loss of future income.

Under such circumstances, with reference to the year of accident, relying upon the guidelines issued by Hon'ble Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru, notional income of the petitioner is taken at the rate of Rs.14,750/- p.m. so that, said fact is taken into consideration for the purpose of calculation of loss income during laid up period and also for the purpose of calculation of loss of future income.

sentences.text: It is admitted fact that, as per the discharge summary marked as Ex.P.10, petitioner was admitted in Sri Venkateswara Institute of Medical Sciences as inpatient from 19.08.2022 to 26.08.2022 i.e., for SCCH-5 7 days
. For the said period he is entitled for the loss of income
as per the guidelines issued by Hon'ble Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru, notional income of the petitioner should be taken into consideration i.e., Rs.14,750/- p.m.

sentences.text: Accordingly petitioner is entitled for the income of said quantum for the period he was admitted as inpatient in the hospital.
So petitioner is entitled for Rs.3,442/- towards loss on income during laid up period.
18. Further admittedly petitioner has exhibited Ex.P.11 medical bills for Rs.6,089/-.
On perusal of the said bills it is clearly stated about spending of amount for this treatment is considered.

Further on perusal of Ex.P.4 in which Doctor who have treated i.e., Dr.K.Lokesh Prasad has categorically stated that, petitioner has sustained grievous injury out of the SCCH-5 accident caused on 18.08.2022.

So as per Ex.P.4 wound certificate, petitioner has sustained lacerated wound over left parietal area, left temporo parietal EDH and left temporo parietal bone depressed fracture, which is Balakrishna Reddy.G vs G. Rakesh on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69941428/
5 grievous in nature.
Further the Investigation Officer has also filed charge sheet against G.Rakesh for the offences punishable under Sec.338 of IPC.

So the said charge sheet materials and evidence of PW-1 and PW-2 clearly states that, petitioner is suffering from grievous injury out of the accident caused in the alleged accident as alleged in the petition and evidence of PW-1.

Accordingly petitioner is entitled for medical expenses of Rs.6,089/-.
19.
Per contra, except oral evidence, respondents have not taken any endeavors to prove the allegations as alleged in the written statement.

In the absence of rebuttal evidence, merely respondents have filed written SCCH-5 statement and they have denied entire case of the petitioner are all not sufficient to disbelieve the petitioner case, because it is bounden duty of them to prove the defence as taken in the written statement.
Accordingly petitioner is entitled for medical bills and other compensation as stated below.

20. Further during the course of arguments, the learned counsel for the petitioner Sri.NKMS argued that, this case is pertaining to head injury sustained by the petitioner and he has no conscious, hence his next friend as well as his brother G.Jayarami Reddy has given his evidence and prays to take into consideration of Rs.15,000/- as notional income and Dr.Shailesh A.V.Rao has also examined, 60%
disability has been given and counsel for the petitioner has filed memo with following rulings;-
SCCH-5 i) 2023 ACJ 490 (Kar) in between Manjunath V/s. Sunil and another ii) 2021 ACJ 2352 (Kar) in between KSRTC V/s. Pankaja H.S. and others iii) Extract of Sec.185 of M.V.Act iv) 2019 ACJ 2852 (Kar) in between Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd, V/s. A.
Rajendra and others.

Per contra, respondent No.2 counsel has orally resisted the said arguments and argued that, the alleged accident was held in the curve road i.e., in the place of curve and there is head on collusion and there is negligency on the part of the petitioner and he has not driving license, RC, hence they have not produced the same and except wound certificate and discharge summary, there is no other records are placed.

Further SCCH-5 counsel for respondent No.2 has filed memo with following rulings;-
i) 2016 ACJ 2003 in between Krishnappa and Others V/s. Rarewala Engineering Works and another ii) ILR 2009 KAR 2921 in between Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s. 6 iv) MFA No.8801/2018 (WC) C/w. MFA No.334/2020 (ECA) in between United India Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s. Nagendra and others 22.

sentences.text: So on careful perusal of the entire rulings and admittedly as per evidence of PW-2 Dr.Shailesh A.V.Rao, SCCH-5 petitioner G.Balakrishna Reddy is unable to give evidence and he has some lacunas in vulbar and other body activities.
Hence, his next friend as well his brother by name G.Jayarami Reddy has examined before the court as PW-1.
Ofcourse in the cross-examination of PW-1 he has admitted following points;
SCCH-5 23.
But the said admissions of the PW-1 have not supports the respondent's case in any manner.

Further in the rulings of the petitioner, their lordship have relied following principles;
a) If any person causing brain injury and aged about 27 years and in case o frontal and temporal lobes, they affects to his memory and tribunal should consider functional disability at 100% etc.,
b) Merely one person has driving vehicle by taking alcohol is not amount to negligency, if the person has consumed alcohol in limit manner as provided under law.
c) The tribunals those have constituted under M.V.Act have got jurisdiction to exercise any cases held within territory of the India.
SCCH-5 24.

The counsel for the petitioner has also relied upon Sec.185 of M.V.Act pertaining to the driving by drunken person or by the person under the influence of drugs and counsel for the petitioner argued that, there is permission under law to consume alcohol upto 30 mg. For 100 ml. of blood.

Here in this case, merely in MLC Extract and other charge sheet materials, Investigation Officer has mentioned about consumption alcohol by the petitioner is not sufficient to disbelieve the case of the petitioner and reject the compensation, because there is no mention in the entire police records nor respondent papers that, how much alcohol has been consumed by the petitioner etc.,
So inview of the ratios laid down by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka relied by the petitioner, I have no hesitation to believe the case of the petitioner as stated supra.

Balakrishna Reddy.G vs G. Rakesh on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69941428/
7 SCCH-5 25.

Ofcourse per contra, in the rulings of the respondent counsel, their lordship held following principles that, 'if the respondent has proved the contributory negligence between both vehicles,
then the tribunals should award the compensation on said principles of contributory negligence etc.,' but the facts and circumstances involved in the rulings of the respondent No.2 are entirely different from the present set of facts, hence they have not supports the respondent's case in any manner.

Accordingly I am of the opinion that, petitioner has categorically, cogently and corroboratively proved his case about causing of the accident as well as suffering head injury out of the accident as mentioned in the charge sheet and in the evidence of PW-1 and PW-2.
SCCH-5 26.
Accordingly, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation as detailed below:-
Sl.No .
Head of Compensation Amount in Rs.
1. Loss of Future Income 5,66,400-00 2. Pain and sufferings 15,000-00 3. Conveyance, nourishment and 15,000-00 attendant charges 4.
Medical Expenses 6,089-00 5. Loss of amenities in life 15,000-00 6. Loss of income during laid up 3,442-00 period Total 6,20,931-00 27.
Accordingly I hold that, the Petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.6,20,931/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization of entire amount.

28. In the case on hand, respondent No.2 being the insurer has issued insurance policy bearing No.2317204465583000001 which is valid for the period SCCH-5 from 12.01.2022 to 11.01.2023, the alleged accident was occurred on 18.08.2022 it reveals that, as on the date of accident, insurance policy was in force.

Hence naturally liability of respondent No.1 shall go against respondent No.2, so that, R2/insurer is directed to deposit the award amount with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. within 60 days from the date of this order.
With these views, I have answered Issue No.2 partly in the affirmative.
29. Issue No.3:

For the reasons assigned to Issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
::ORDER

: :
Balakrishna Reddy.G vs G. Rakesh on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69941428/
8
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.6,20,931/- (Rupees Six Lakhs Twenty Thousand Nine Hundred Thirty One Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
from the date of petition till its realization.

SCCH-5 The Respondent No.2 shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.
The Petitioner is entitled to get release 60% of the award amount through e-payment directly to his account on furnishing the Bank A/c details along with address proof and remaining 40% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any of the Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in his name.
The Advocate Fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

16. As per his case, he was doing agricultural work and doing milk vending business, thereby earning Rs.30,000/- p.m., to prove the said fact, there are no SCCH-5 documents on record.
Under such circumstances, with reference to the year of accident, relying upon the guidelines issued by Hon'ble Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru, notional income of the petitioner is taken at the rate of Rs.14,750/- p.m. so that, said fact is taken into consideration for the purpose of calculation of loss income during laid up period and also for the purpose of calculation of loss of future income.
. For the said period he is entitled for the loss of income
Further the Investigation Officer has also filed charge sheet against G.Rakesh for the offences punishable under Sec.338 of IPC.
So the said charge sheet materials and evidence of PW-1 and PW-2 clearly states that, petitioner is suffering from grievous injury out of the accident caused in the alleged accident as alleged in the petition and evidence of PW-1.
Per contra, except oral evidence, respondents have not taken any endeavors to prove the allegations as alleged in the written statement.
In the absence of rebuttal evidence, merely respondents have filed written SCCH-5 statement and they have denied entire case of the petitioner are all not sufficient to disbelieve the petitioner case, because it is bounden duty of them to prove the defence as taken in the written statement.
